articles.title: Latest Heisman Trophy 2026 Odds as Trinidad Chambliss Rises, Marcel Reed Falls
articles.summary: Nearing the end of a very notable Week 3 in the 2026 college football season, the early Heisman race is starting to take shape.
articles.body:
Nearing the end of a very notable Week 3 in the 2026 college football season, the early Heisman race is starting to take shape.

In the latest odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , Trinidad Chambliss surged to the top of the list during a red-hot start in Ole Miss' game against LSU.

Chambliss settled at +310 (bet $100 to win $310) as the favorite after leading Ole Miss to a 32-24 win over Lane Kiffin and LSU.

He took over as the favorite from Miami quarterback Darian Mensah, who was the favorite earlier in the day at +240 before sliding to +390. Quarterbacks Arch Manning and Kamario Taylor and wide receivers Jeremiah Smith and Malachi Toney were also high on the list.

Based on Saturday's results, the biggest loser in the race is Marcel Reed after Texas A&M was upset by Kentucky at Kyle Field.

Here is the current top 10 in the Heisman race by betting odds.

Reed didn't have great support coming into this week, but his odds now sit at 125-1. He finished 26-of-49 for 236 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions against Kentucky.

There's still plenty of time for the Aggies to build themselves back into a playoff contender, but it's safe to assume the Heisman won't be making its way to College Station later this year.

Mensah's separation from the pack comes after he started 24-of-24 in Miami's 33-20 win over Wake Forest on Friday night. He did end up throwing four incompletions in the game, lowering his season-long completion percentage to a pedestrian 89.9 on 79 attempts.

One of the big reasons Mensah has had so much success early in the season is his rapport with Toney. The Hurricanes star wideout has jumped into a tie for second place in the Heisman odds thanks to leading FBS in receptions (28), receiving yards (444) and receiving touchdowns (five).

Based on last week's odds , Arch Manning has seen a lot of movement. Coming out of Texas' dramatic win over Ohio State, he was at +2500 and is now down +1200.

Manning's gain appears to have negatively impacted Smith, who was +440 last week. The Buckeyes standout did make history on Saturday by becoming their all-time leader in receiving yards in a 59-3 win over Kent State.

It is interesting that Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin is well behind Smith in the odds because normally the edge would go to the signal-caller, but Smith's reputation and dominance has been so well established that he is viewed as the primary engine for the offense.

Another player who fell from where they were perched last week is Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton. He was at +2200 after a 70-20 victory over Western Kentucky, but now sits outside the top 10 at +4000.

Stockton wasn't asked to do a lot on Saturday against Arkansas, but he made his opportunities count. He went 10-of-13 for 147 yards and one touchdown through the air, along with 97 rushing yards on seven carries in a 45-17 road victory.

All eyes are now on Chambliss to take control of the race after throwing 363 passing yards and three total touchdowns in Ole Miss' upset win against No. 7 LSU.

articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “My family kept me grounded when the whole world was screaming my name.” - How Ryan Coleman-Williams turned unconditional family backing into college football superstardom
articles.summary: International Sports News: Ryan Coleman-Williams was already one of the biggest names in Alabama high school football when he made a decision that changed his path. The Saraland.
articles.body: Ryan Coleman-Williams was already one of the biggest names in Alabama high school football when he made a decision that changed his path. The Saraland star left high school a year early, moved from the 2025 recruiting class to 2024 and joined Alabama at just 17. The move came with plenty of attention, but his family had been part of his football journey long before he reached Tuscaloosa. His father, Ryan Williams Sr., had played college football, while his mother, Tiffany Coleman, and his grandparents helped give him the support and structure he needed from a young age.How Ryan Coleman-Williams and Ryan Williams Sr. built their football connectionFootball was familiar territory in the Williams family. Ryan Williams Sr. played at Auburn after a standout high school career at B.C. Rain in Mobile. He later transferred to Copiah-Lincoln Community College and finished his college career at Louisiana Tech. His playing career gave him a clear understanding of the demands that came with trying to reach the next level.But Ryan Coleman-Williams’ development was not only about his father’s football background. ESPN reported that Williams lived with his paternal grandparents, Robert and Catherine Williams, while his father was away at college. His mother, Tiffany Coleman, also spoke about the role the family played in shaping his personality.“He’s an old soul,” Coleman told ESPN. “People are like, ‘He’s so mature to be 17.’ His grandparents had a lot to do with that. His maturity and foundation came from them.”That family support became especially important as Williams’ football career began moving faster than most teenagers could imagine.At Saraland High School, he became one of the most productive players in the state. Alabama’s official profile says he had 198 receptions for 3,486 yards and 49 receiving touchdowns during his high school career. He also rushed for 1,082 yards and 25 touchdowns.Why Ryan Williams reclassified from 2025 to 2024Williams originally belonged to the 2025 recruiting class. He had already committed to Alabama, but in 2023 he and his family decided that he would finish high school early and join the Crimson Tide sooner than planned.The decision was not made suddenly. ESPN reported that Williams told Saraland coach Jeff Kelly about the move in July 2023, although the decision was kept private while the team continued its season. Williams officially announced the reclassification in December.Kelly said the family handled the decision carefully because Williams did not want it to become a distraction for his teammates.“I think it speaks volumes about who he is,” Kelly told ESPN. “He didn’t want it to be out there because he didn’t want it to be a distraction for his teammates. We had a team that had a chance to win another state title. He and his family did a tremendous job keeping that decision private.”The timing also made sense from a football point of view. Williams had already achieved almost everything possible at the high school level. In 2023, he helped Saraland win another Class 6A state title and finished his high school career with huge numbers.The Alabama Sports Writers Association later named him Mr. Football for the second straight year, making him the first two-time winner of the award.What Ryan Williams did at Alabama at only 17Joining Alabama meant stepping into a completely different level of football. Williams was only 17 during his freshman season, while competing against players who were several years older.He showed that the age gap did not stop him.In September 2024, Williams caught a 75-yard touchdown pass from Jalen Milroe against Georgia in front of more than 100,000 fans at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Alabama won 41-34, and the play became one of the defining moments of Williams’ first college season.Alabama’s official records from that season show just how fast he adjusted. He finished his freshman campaign with 48 catches for 865 yards and eight touchdowns, according to the university’s later player profile. He also earned freshman All-America recognition.The early success was not completely unexpected. Before he even played a college game, Alabama had already listed Williams as a five-star recruit and one of the country’s top receiving prospects. The university said he was among the five-star players added to its 2024 recruiting class.How Ryan Williams’ family stayed part of his riseThe numbers tell only part of Williams’ story. His family had been around him throughout the long process that took him from Saraland to Alabama.That was clear when he officially signed with Alabama in February 2024. Local outlet Call News published a photograph of Williams with his father Ryan Sr., mother Tiffany Coleman, grandmother Catherine Williams and stepmother Cortney Williams at the signing ceremony.His grandmother has also spoken about how unusual his focus was even as a young child. She recalled that when Williams was in kindergarten, he was already eager to help teachers while other children were playing.That same focus later showed up on the football field.Williams did not have to wait until college to become a star. At Saraland, he won Alabama Mr. Football twice and became one of the most closely watched high school players in the state. His family then supported a difficult decision to leave school early and take on college football at an age when most players are still preparing for their final high school season.That is what makes Ryan Williams’ rise from Saraland to Alabama especially striking. His story is not only about spectacular catches or becoming a college football name at 17. It is also about a young player making an unusually early jump while having his parents, grandparents and family around him throughout the process.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Champions return, 314 debutants arrive: Inside India’s 500-plus Asian Games campaign
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Hoping to build on the historic campaign three years back at Hangzhou, India begins its campaign at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with a .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Hoping to build on the historic campaign three years back at Hangzhou, India begins its campaign at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with a 500-plus athlete contingent, aiming to better the 106-medal tally racked up at the last Games.While the build-up to the Games has been marred by mismanagement, an accommodation crisis and the threat of a typhoon looming large over the Japanese prefecture, for the athletes, once the Games begin, it will be, as the adage goes, ‘game mode on’.The 500-plus athlete Indian contingent comprises a sizeable group of returning champions and experienced campaigners. 314 of those athletes are preparing for their first appearance at the continental event.Interestingly, women athletes make up 46.7% of the contingent. At 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is the youngest member. Equestrian rider Shruti Vora, 55, is the oldest.India will compete in 256 events across 36 of the 43 sports at Aichi-Nagoya, with the Games beginning on September 19 and running until October 4.Avinash Sable, returning from a year-long injury, will try to defend his men's 3000m steeplechase title, while Tajinderpal Singh Toor returns in the men's shot put. Parul Chaudhary will be another athlete trying to defend her women's 5000m crown, while India's men's 4x400m relay team will also go into the Games as defending champions.In badminton, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will aim to defend their men's doubles title. Their gold in Hangzhou was India's first Asian Games title in the event.Indian compound archers swept all five gold medals in the discipline at Hangzhou, and returning champion Jyothi Surekha Vennam will be the fulcrum around whom India's archery campaign will revolve.Then there are athletes whose Asian Games story is still waiting for a first chapter.Mirabai Chanu’s missing Asian Games medalMirabai Chanu has won a world title, Olympic silver and Commonwealth Games gold. The Asian Games medal remains missing from her collection.The 32-year-old will lead India's four-member weightlifting team in Aichi-Nagoya, with Gyaneshwari Yadav, Seram Nirupama Devi and Harjinder Kaur completing the squad.Chanu missed the 2018 Asian Games because of injury and did not compete at Hangzhou. Now, after a career that has already included a world championship title, an Olympic medal and multiple Commonwealth Games titles, the Asian Games is the major multi-sport medal still absent from her cabinet.Anahat arrives as a world junior championAnahat Singh is another young Indian athlete arriving in Japan with a title already behind her.The 18-year-old is a World Junior Squash Champion and has made the transition from junior squash to the senior international circuit at a young age.She is part of India's eight-member squash team in Aichi-Nagoya. Joshana Chinappa, Tanvi Khanna and Shameena Riaz are the other members of the women's squad, while Abhay Singh, Velavan Senthilkumar, Veer Chotrani and Suraj Kumar Chand make up the men's team.Squash was among India's gold-medal sports at Hangzhou.Manu Bhaker, Aishwary Pratap and a large shooting groupShooting will once again be one of the major sports to follow, with 27 events on India's programme.The contingent had bagged 22 medals at Hangzhou, including seven golds.Manu Bhaker returns in the women's squad alongside the in-form Esha Singh, Rahi Sarnobat, Elavenil Valarivan, Ashi Chouksey, Suruchi Singh and Tilottama Sen.The men's group includes Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Rudrankksh Patil and Anish Bhanwala.There will also be a sizable shotgun shooters' bunch, with the veteran Mairaj Ahmed Khan leading the pack alongside Kynan Chenai, Shapath Bharadwaj and Ahvar Rizvi. Neeru Dhanda, Manisha Keer, Maheshwari Chauhan and Parinaaz Dhaliwal are also part of the shotgun group.Neeraj Chopra, meanwhile, will not be in Japan. The javelin thrower, who defended his Asian Games title in Hangzhou, is missing the 2026 Games after an ankle ligament injury during training.Athletics remains the biggest groupAthletics has the largest athlete representation, with 78 competitors, and also has the biggest programme with 43 events. They had bagged a total of 29 medals, including six golds, at Hangzhou, and the expectation will be to go many a medal better this time around.Alongside Sable, Toor and Parul are names such as Gulveer Singh, Animesh Kujur, Harita Bhadra, Jyothi Yarraji, Murali Sreeshankar, Praveen Chithravel and Tejaswin Shankar.Hockey: defending champions and a women’s team on the riseThe men's hockey team goes into Aichi-Nagoya as the defending Asian Games champion, but its recent World Cup campaign has left a different question hanging over the side.India won gold in Hangzhou in 2023, beating Japan 5-1 in the final, and the title also secured direct qualification for the Paris Olympics. The team now has another Olympic berth at stake in Japan, with the Asian Games gold medallist earning direct qualification for Los Angeles 2028.The women's team comes to Japan with a more encouraging recent result.India finished fifth at the 2026 Women's Hockey World Cup, their best finish at the tournament in 52 years. The campaign included a 2-2 draw against China, the 2024 Olympic silver medallists, a result that carried particular weight after India's 4-0 defeat to the same opposition in the Hangzhou Asian Games semifinal.The women's team has not won the Asian Games since 1982, and gold in Aichi-Nagoya would also bring direct qualification for the 2028 Olympics. Salima Tete will captain the side, with Savita Punia, Lalremsiami, Navneet Kaur, Deepika and Nikki Pradhan among the experienced players in the squad.Cricket brings another set of familiar namesIndia's men's T20 team is led by Shreyas Iyer and includes Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan, Shivam Dube, Tilak Varma, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Jasprit Bumrah and Arshdeep Singh.Sooryavanshi is also part of the squad.Harmanpreet Kaur leads the women's side, with Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh and Renuka Thakur among the selected players.India won both the men's and women's T20 gold medals at Hangzhou.There will also be Indian participation in four esports events - eFootball, Puyo Puyo Champions, League of Legends and Pokemon Unite.Haryana leads the state-wise numbersHaryana has the largest representation with 96 athletes.Maharashtra follows with 49, Tamil Nadu 37, Punjab 35, Manipur 34, Uttar Pradesh 32 and Delhi 30.Karnataka, Kerala and Madhya Pradesh have 24 athletes each.The representation stretches across the country, with athletes also coming from Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Arunachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Mizoram, Nagaland, Puducherry, Tripura, Sikkim, Ladakh and Lakshadweep.The support structure behind the contingent is spread across several programmes. National Coaching Camps account for 134 athletes, followed by TOPS Development with 78 and TOPS Core with 77. Khelo India has 65 athletes, TAGG 48 and National Centres of Excellence 25.Aichi-Nagoya therefore brings together a group that already knows the Asian Games podium and another that has never experienced it.Mirabai Chanu still has one major medal to add. Anahat Singh arrives as a world junior champion. Manu Bhaker and Aishwary Pratap lead another large shooting group, while Sable, Toor, Parul, Jyothi and Satwik-Chirag return as defending champions.And around them are 314 first-timers, spread across 256 events in 36 sports.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Leeds United host Crystal Palace at Elland Road on Sunday, with only champions Arsenal and Manchester City above Daniel Farke's side in the Premier League table after four games.

The Whites have won their last two matches, including a 4-1 thrashing of Newcastle United , and have been beaten only once in their last 13 league fixtures. Crystal Palace, who have taken just three points from four games under new head coach Pierre Sage, suffered a gut-wrenching 3-2 defeat to Ipswich Town last weekend but responded with a comfortable 4-0 win over Lech Poznan in their opening Europa League fixture in midweek. Leeds won 4-1 in this exact fixture last season, though the sides' most recent meeting, in March, ended goalless at Selhurst Park.

Leeds United vs Crystal Palace – Match preview and team news

Referee: Adam Herczeg (making his Premier League debut)

Last meeting: Crystal Palace 0-0 Leeds United (Premier League, 15 March 2026, Selhurst Park)

Harry Wilson is sidelined with a quad injury, while Joe Rodon (hamstring) and Mateo Joseph (knee) remain in the treatment room. Farke could name an unchanged side, with James Justin , Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemovic continuing at centre-back and Jayden Bogle and Gabriel Gudmundsson as wing-backs.

Axel Disasi begins a three-match suspension following his red card against Ipswich, while Dean Henderson (ankle), Jean-Philippe Mateta (hamstring) and Chadi Riad (knee) all remain out. Sage will decide between Takehiro Tomiyasu and Jaydee Canvot to complete the back three, while Ismaila Sarr — who made his first appearance of the season as a substitute in midweek — is "maybe" ready to start, according to the manager, but not fit enough to last the full 90 minutes.

Leeds have won two and drawn two of their four Premier League matches, remaining unbeaten in the league this season, and Dominic Calvert-Lewin has scored in each of his last five home league appearances.

Palace have lost three of their four league games, with their only win coming at Fulham , and have conceded the most goals (11) and faced the most touches in their own box of any Premier League side so far this season.

Leeds United predicted XI (3-5-2): Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Stach , Ampadu , Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Calvert-Lewin, Okafor

Crystal Palace predicted XI (3-4-2-1): Benitez; Tomiyasu, Richards, Ahanor; Khalaili, Timber, Wharton, Mitchell; Sarr, Pino; Strand Larsen

How to watch Leeds United vs Crystal Palace?

The match will be broadcast live in the United Kingdom on Sky Sports.

articles.title: Five takeaways from Utah football's shutout win over Utah State
articles.summary: A stifling defense and Braden Pegan’s explosive perimeter play powered the Utes to a dominant shutout, providing a perfect momentum boost before their highly...
articles.body:
Utah took care of business against Utah State , shutting out the Aggies 33-0 and moving to 3-0 heading into Big 12 play.

It wasn't quite the offensive explosion we saw against Idaho or Arkansas , especially after halftime, but Utah controlled the game from the start. The Utes finished with 480 yards of offense while holding Utah State to just 188.

Braden Pegan was a mismatch against Utah State's secondary.

Pegan caught three passes on Utah's opening drive, including a 28-yard touchdown on third-and-14. By halftime, he already had seven catches for 113 yards and two touchdowns. He finished with eight catches for 122 yards and two scores.

Utah State kept giving him one-on-one opportunities, and Utah kept making them pay.

"If you're going to play him one-on-one, that's kind of what's going to happen," Devon Dampier said after the game. "The ball is going to find him, and plays are going to be made."

There is not much else to say at this point.

Utah's defense has been dominant through three weeks, and Saturday might have been its most complete performance yet.

The Utes pitched their first shutout since beating Cal 35-0 in October of 2019. Utah State finished with just 188 total yards, 10 first downs, and went 4-of-14 on third down.

The defensive line was creating pressure. The secondary once again made throwing the football hard for the Aggies.

Utah's secondary has been one of the best parts of this team through three games, and that continued today.

Brosterhous finished just 15-of-29 passing for 130 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. That is a 51.7% completion rate and only 4.5 yards per pass attempt.

Rabbit Evans came away with a big interception in the end zone when Utah State finally put together one of its best drives of the afternoon.

Coming off a game where Utah broke up 13 passes against Arkansas, the secondary keeps showing up.

The front seven kept Brosterhous contained

This was another really good game from Utah's defensive front.

Utah finished with four sacks and held the Aggies to just 58 rushing yards on 25 attempts. Utah State picked up only one rushing first down all game.

A big part was how Utah handled Brosterhous.

He entered the game as Utah State's leading rusher and had just run for 81 yards against Washington. Utah clearly knew his legs were one of the biggest things it had to account for.

Brosterhous carried it 17 times Saturday and finished with just 17 yards.

The defensive line kept him uncomfortable in the pocket and forced him to move. Still, when he did escape, Utah's linebackers did a really good job containing him and keeping any scrambles from becoming big plays.

Utah State never established an interior run game either.

After holding Arkansas to 61 rushing yards last week, Utah has now allowed just 119 combined rushing yards over its last two games.

The second half felt like Utah started coasting

Utah went into halftime up 26-0 and was completely in control.

Then the offense lost some of the creativity we saw early.

Utah scored just seven points after halftime, and that came on Daniel Bray 's 63-yard touchdown run. Outside of that one explosive play, there wasn't a whole lot happening offensively. Maybe that was intentional.

Utah had the game under control, the defense wasn't giving Utah State anything, and Big 12 play starts next week at Iowa State. McGiven had no reason to keep opening up the playbook and showing everything Utah has.

But the interior run game is something to watch.

Wayshawn Parker finished with just 30 yards on 10 carries, and Utah's overall rushing numbers look better because of Bray's 63-yard touchdown.

That does not erase what Utah has done offensively through three weeks, but it is probably the biggest thing I would like to see cleaned up heading into conference play.

Utah did exactly what it needed to do Saturday.

It handled the mismatch with Pegan, played elite defense, dominated Utah State's run game, and walked away with a shutout.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Experts Top 25 Rankings After Week 3
articles.summary: With fewer cupcakes and more conference matchups in Week 3, more volatility in this week's Top 25 was inevitable.
articles.body:
With fewer cupcakes and more conference matchups in Week 3, more volatility in this week's Top 25 was inevitable.

The big upset of the day came during the afternoon slate when Kentucky upended Texas A&M at Kyle Field, throwing an early wrench into the SEC landscape.

Louisville handing SMU its first loss of the season could also be an important result in the race to the ACC championship game. After playing Ole Miss tough in Week 1, the Cardinals are one to watch in the coming weeks.

All of that was the appetizer to Lane Kiffin's highly anticipated return to Oxford, as Ole Miss came out on top in a 32-24 thriller.

Now it's time for Bleacher Report's updated top 25 ranking, with the college football writing staff of David Kenyon, Adam Kramer, Joel Reuter and Brad Shepard making up our voting panel.

Week 3 Result: LOSS vs. Kentucky (21-31) Next Week: at LSU

After a 48-20 blowout against Arizona State last week on the strength of 24 fourth-quarter points, the Aggies were simply outplayed by Kentucky for three quarters. A 28-7 deficit proved too steep to overcome in a major blow to their College Football Playoff hopes. Marcel Reed threw two interceptions, falling to 2-4 in his career in games when he throws multiple picks, including both of the Aggies' losses a year ago.

Week 3 Result: WIN at Auburn (44-39) Next Week: vs. Ole Miss

The Gators blew out Florida Atlantic (66-21) and Campbell (52-3) to start the season, but earned their spot in the rankings with a road win against Auburn to kick off SEC play. Jadan Baugh shouldered the offensive load once again, recording 26 carries for 162 yards and three touchdowns for his third straight 100-yard rushing performance. Defensively, the Gators managed to contain dual-threat quarterback Byrum Brown. He finished with 271 passing yards and 65 rushing yards while throwing an interception and averaging 3.6 yards per carry.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Stanford (35-7) Next Week: vs. William & Mary

The Blue Devils have quietly played one of the more balanced schedules in the nation so far this year, with victories over Tulane, Illinois and Stanford. Running back Nate Sheppard entered play on Saturday with 434 total yards and five touchdowns. He further padded those gaudy stats with 23 carries for 154 yards and three scores, including a two-yard receiving touchdown. That Nov. 14 game at Miami is looking more and more interesting with each passing week.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. UTEP (52-17) Next Week: vs. Iowa

The Wolverines fell behind early with a lost fumble and a turnover on downs in their first two offensive possessions and led just 17-14 at halftime, but they blew the game open with 28 unanswered points in the third quarter. Bryce Underwood (19/25, 233 yards, 2 TD) had his best game of the season under center, while Savion Hiter (11 carries, 62 yards, 2 TD) and Jordan Marshall (12 carries, 59 yards, 1 TD) led a rushing attack that finished with 185 yards on 42 carries.

21. Kansas State (3-0, Previous Rank: NR)

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Tulane (31-20) Next Week: at Cincinnati

Avery Johnson tallied 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns while completing 21-of-28 pass attempts for 227 yards. The Wildcats piled up 428 total yards of offense against a solid Tulane defense. On defense, the Wildcats logged 12 tackles for loss and six sacks while allowing just 2.9 yards per carry to a Green Wave offense that had 212 rushing yards in Week 2.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Troy (27-17) Next Week: at Mississippi State

Only six different players recorded offensive touches for Missouri in a less-than-dominant performance against Troy, where they were 26.5-point favorites. Jamal Roberts (22 carries, 128 yards, 1 TD; 2 catches, 13 yards) accounted for more than half of Mizzou's 230 total yards. The Tigers punted seven times in a game where they never found an offensive rhythm outside of a 24-point second quarter that proved to be the difference.

19. Virginia Tech (3-0, Previous Rank: 24)

Week 3 Result: WIN at Maryland (35-26) Next Week: at Boston College

After blowout victories over VMI and Old Dominion, the Hokies logged an impressive road victory against Maryland on Saturday night to solidify their status as a nationally relevant team heading into ACC conference play. Ethan Grunkemeyer completed 31 of 39 passes for 314 yards and three touchdowns. Virginia Tech built a 35-14 lead that held up down the stretch when Maryland responded to a pair of punts with touchdowns of their own to make things close.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Northern Iowa (55-0) Next Week: at Michigan

After a grind-it-out battle in the Cy-Hawk rivalry against Iowa State last week, the Hawkeyes had far less trouble with a different in-state foe on Saturday as they steamrolled Northern Iowa. Xavier Williams, Braeden Jackson and Nathan McNeil each broke 100 yards rushing. Iowa finished with a staggering 422 yards and six touchdowns on 41 carries. Hank Brown also went a perfect 12-of-12 for 153 yards and two touchdowns in what has been an improved passing game in the early going.

17. Mississippi State (3-0, Previous Rank: 25)

Week 3 Result: WIN at South Carolina (41-34) Next Week: vs. Missouri

Kamario Taylor continued his breakout season with a second straight road win following a Week 2 victory at Minnesota, completing 18-of-26 pass attempts for 251 yards and four touchdowns while chipping in another 33 yards rushing. The Bulldogs trailed 16-0 early in the second quarter and 23-14 at halftime, but ripped off 27 unanswered points coming out of the break to put things out of reach. Will it be enough for them to earn a spot in the AP poll for the first time since 2022?

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Buffalo (55-13) Next Week: vs. Wisconsin

A relentless Nittany Lions rushing attack piled up 41 carries for 304 yards and five touchdowns. Rocco Becht added 212 yards and two scores through the air in a gaudy performance by the Penn State offense. They have outscored Marshall, Temple and Buffalo by a 127-22 margin in a relatively easy 3-0 start that has given Matt Campbell's new-look roster a chance to build some confidence and cohesion heading into conference play.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. SMU (41-31) Next Week: vs. Wake Forest

Trailing 31-28 early in the fourth quarter, Louisville used a 4-play, 75-yard touchdown drive to take the lead, forced a turnover on downs and then made it a two-possession game with a 3-play, 64-yard drive before the defense locked down the win with a forced fumble and an interception. Lincoln Kienholz (177 passing yards, 42 rushing yards, 3 TD) continues to be one of the early breakout stars of the 2026 season, while Keyjuan Brown (10 carries, 163 yards, 2 TD) was the headliner out of the backfield.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Kennesaw State (42-9) Next Week: vs. Texas

True freshman Faizon Brandon continues to look like a future star for the Volunteers, showcasing his dual-threat talents once again against Kennesaw State with 178 passing yards, 47 rushing yards and two touchdowns. The Tennessee rushing attack finished with 41 carries for 268 yards and four touchdowns. They cruised to victory after building a 35-3 lead through three quarters. A different level of test awaits next weekend when the Longhorns come to Knoxville.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Utah State (33-0) Next Week: at Iowa State

The Utes forced almost as many punts (8) as they allowed first downs (10) en route to their first shutout against an FBS opponent since 2019. They have now outscored the opposition 142-24 during their 3-0 start to the year. Devon Dampier (22/32, 253 yards, 2 TD) and Braden Pegan (8 catches, 122 yards, 2 TD) had a terrific connection through the air, while the running game accounted for 286 yards on just 25 carries.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Houston (28-26) Next Week: vs. Sam Houston

The Red Raiders' defense kept Houston quarterback Connor Weigman out of the end zone on a two-point conversion attempt that would have tied the game with 49 seconds remaining, surviving what currently stands as the only game on their schedule against a ranked opponent. Cameron Dickey (16 carries, 65 yards, 1 TD) and J'Koby Williams (7 carries, 62 yards, 1 TD) both found the end zone during the second half to anchor the Texas Tech offense.

Week 3 Result: WIN at Colorado State (41-23) Next Week: BYE

Colorado State had no answer for the BYU running game, as the Cougars carried the ball 41 times for 332 yards and five touchdowns. LJ Martin (15 carries, 176 yards, 3 TD) led the way offensively, while Bear Bachmeier had 227 yards and an interception while only attempting 16 passes. The Cougars carried a 38-7 lead into the fourth quarter in a road game against a Rams team that had posted two lopsided victories to start the year.

Week 3 Result: LOSS at Ole Miss (24-32) Next Week: vs. Texas A&M

LSU looked headed for a blowout loss when Ole Miss made it 24-7 at halftime with a flawlessly executed two-minute drill, but the Tigers stormed back, as a 23-yard field goal with 11:21 remaining in the fourth quarter made it 24-24. The defense surrendered a 13-play, 74-yard touchdown drive on the subsequent possession, while Sam Leavitt led a 14-play, 69-yard march of his own into the red zone. However, his fourth-and-goal pass attempt was tipped at the line and picked off in the end zone to leave the comeback six yards short.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Florida State (50-36) Next Week: vs. South Carolina

The Crimson Tide put together three touchdown drives inside the final 10 minutes of the first half to turn a 21-6 deficit into a 26-21 lead, then put points on the board in each of their first four possessions of the second half to take control of the game. Keelon Russell completed 23-of-30 pass attempts for 320 yards and three touchdowns in his best aerial performance of the young season, adding 56 rushing yards and another score. The defense had three sacks, three interceptions and allowed 2.7 yards per carry.

Week 3 Result: WIN at Rutgers (42-35) Next Week: vs. Oregon

Allowing 35 points and 460 yards to a Rutgers team that lost to UMass in Week 1 is not exactly one for USC's highlight reel, but a 4-0 start and a Big Ten road win is still plenty to hang their hat on. Jayden Maiava (20/32, 277 yards, 2 TD) had a less efficient game than he did in three excellent performances to open the year, while King Miller (16 carries, 102 yards, 1 TD) helped provide some balance and the defense came away with a pair of interceptions to offset the yardage allowed.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Kent State (59-3) Next Week: vs. Illinois

Julian Sayin (18-of-22, 241 yards, 2 TD), Bo Jackson (11 carries, 73 yards, 1 TD) and Jeremiah Smith (5 catches, 85 yards) all put together strong individual performances in a palette cleanser game for the Buckeyes following their Week 2 loss to Texas. The defense forced three turnovers, allowed 134 total yards and surrendered just six first downs in a dominant performance across the board that will be the springboard into Big Ten play.

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Western Kentucky (38-0) Next Week: vs. Northwestern

The Hoosiers didn't put points on the scoreboard until the 10:00 mark in the second quarter after missing a field goal on their opening drive, but that's about the only hole to poke in a lopsided victory where they outgained Western Kentucky 513-186 in total yardage while the defense pitched a shutout for the second week in a row. Josh Hoover continued his strong start by completing 18-of-24 pass attempts for 273 yards and two touchdowns, while Turbo Richard (15 carries, 149 yards, 1 TD) and Lee Beebe Jr. (17 carries, 50 yards, 2 TD) both did significant damage on the ground.

5. Ole Miss Rebels (3-0, Previous Rank: 8)

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. LSU (32-24) Next Week: at Florida

After 17 unanswered points from LSU coming out of halftime saw a 24-7 Ole Miss lead evaporate into a tie game, Trinidad Chambliss responded with a 13-play, 74-yard drive that was punctuated by a 14-yard touchdown run from the Rebels star quarterback.

The defense bent on the subsequent LSU possession but didn't break, holding on in a first-and-goal to eventually come away with the game-ending interception on a tipped fourth down pass.

Chambliss finished with 363 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown, adding a signature win to his Heisman Trophy candidacy.

4. Miami Hurricanes (3-0, Previous Rank: 3)

Week 3 Result: WIN at Wake Forest (33-20) Next Week: vs. Central Michigan

Darian Mensah completed his first 24 attempts to set a new ACC record for consecutive completions. He finished 30-of-34 for 220 yards and three touchdowns as the Hurricanes came out on top in their first legitimate test of the season.

A pair of Wake Forest touchdowns in the second half made things interesting, cutting a 31-7 deficit down to a 31-20 game with 14:56 remaining in the fourth quarter, but the Miami defense clamped down with a safety, two turnovers on downs and an interception over the Demon Deacons' final four possessions.

Malachi Toney (12 catches, 114 yards, 1 TD) and Mark Fletcher Jr. (16 carries, 85 yards, 1 TD) once again had standout days offensively, while the defensive front held Wake Forest to 22 rushing yards on 16 carries.

3. Notre Dame Fighting Irish (3-0, Previous Rank: 2)

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. Michigan State (27-10) Next Week: at Purdue

CJ Carr (18/24, 234 yards) and Micah Gilbert (8 catches, 170 yards) had a big day through the air. The running game finished the job with 161 yards and three scores, but the Notre Dame defense slammed the door after halftime.

Michigan State mustered only three punts and an interception in the second half. The Spartans were limited to 167 total yards and two turnovers.

The Fighting Irish also dominated the time of possession battle (37:02 to 22:58), running 22 more plays than Michigan State and fully controlling a game that was not as close as the final score suggests.

2. Georgia Bulldogs (3-0, Previous Rank: 4)

Week 3 Result: WIN at Arkansas (45-17) Next Week: vs. Oklahoma

The Bulldogs were leading 38-3 with 150 total yards allowed on defense before Arkansas closed out the game with consecutive 75-yard touchdown drives, so the performance was even more dominant than the final score suggests.

Gunner Stockton had 147 passing yards, 97 rushing yards and one touchdown in another abbreviated outing under center. Chauncey Bowens had three rushing touchdowns and the Bulldogs' defensive front surrendered 17 rushing yards on 20 carries.

Next week's game against Oklahoma will be their first major test, as they face a Sooner team looking to make a statement after a disappointing start.

1. Texas Longhorns (3-0, Previous Rank: 1)

Week 3 Result: WIN vs. UTSA (30-6) Next Week: at Tennessee

With veteran quarterback Owen McCown and the No. 55 spot in The Athletic's ranking of all 138 FBS teams, UTSA was by no means a cupcake game for the Longhorns. They managed to avoid a letdown coming off last weekend's emotional comeback victory over Ohio State.

Arch Manning had 164 passing yards and two touchdowns. He also chipped in 50 rushing yards as Texas piled up 228 yards on 48 carries to dominate time of possession and keep the Roadrunners from finding any momentum.

McCown, who threw for 2,995 yards and 30 touchdowns last year, was limited to 14-of-23 passing for 70 yards and an interception. Now, the SEC grind begins for the nation's No. 1 team.

Others receiving votes: Oregon, SMU, Oklahoma

articles.title: Everything Lane Kiffin Said After LSU Lost to Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss in Revenge Game
articles.summary: LSU head coach Lane Kiffin reacted to the No. 7 Tigers' 32-24 defeat at the hands of No. 8 Ole Miss and quarterback Trinidad Chambliss on Saturday night.
articles.body:
LSU head coach Lane Kiffin reacted to the No. 7 Tigers' 32-24 defeat at the hands of No. 8 Ole Miss and quarterback Trinidad Chambliss on Saturday night.

"Credit to them, players made plays," Kiffin said during his press conference after the game (0:02 mark). "That's what all week my biggest fear every minute was, when the game is at the end and Trinidad has the ball in his hand. The guy made a lot of plays during the game and did a great job, that's why I said he's the hardest player to play in America. He showed up great today."

Kiffin also revealed that he was glad to finish playing his former team for the first time, as he previously left Ole Miss to sign a seven-year contract worth $91 million with LSU during the 2025 season.

"I was thinking that all week," Kiffin told reporters (2:15 mark). "Especially today. I would've said that in a win or a loss. That was really emotional driving in on the buses for a lot of reasons. I'm not saying this because I lost, I would've said this anyway. It was a lot of emotions of gratefulness for this place and for this six years. It went well beyond football."

"It was just a lot of gratitude for this place and the people that changed my life way bigger than winning a football game," he added.

Kiffin discussed the message he has for his team moving forward as well.

"The game could've kept going the way it was, so I was glad that they battled back in there," Kiffin said (5:51 mark). "Really strained during that third quarter, early fourth quarter. Kind of had them on the ropes. So, we're 0-1 in SEC play. Whether win or loss, I was already ready for that of knowing it feels like we've already played a season with so much emotion of the games. The first and third games, all of this stuff."

"Now we're right back to where we've always been and have eight SEC games to play," he added. "So, there's a lot of football left. Go back home next week and get a win."

The Rebels started off strong on Saturday, jumping out to a 17-0 lead in the second quarter.

While LSU was finally able to get on the board with a short touchdown run by Dilin Jones, Ole Miss found the end zone once again to maintain a 24-7 edge at halftime.

The Rebels appeared to be continuing their momentum in the second half after forcing the Tigers to punt on their first drive of the third quarter, but Chambliss subsequently threw an interception.

Kiffin's team capitalized on the opportunity with touchdowns on their next two drives, cutting the deficit to 24-21.

LSU finally tied the game again with a 23-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter.

Ole Miss quickly responded, going on a 74-yard drive that ended with a touchdown run by Chambliss. Head coach Pete Golding's squad also added a successful two-point conversion.

LSU was able to drive down to Ole Miss' five-yard line on its final possession of the game, but a pass from Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt was intercepted on fourth down to seal the final result.

Chambliss finished 33-of-48 for 363 yards and two touchdowns while getting picked off once. He also rushed for one score.

As for Leavitt, he completed 59.3 percent of his passes for 158 yards and one touchdown compared to one interception. He picked up 63 yards and a touchdown on the ground as well.

LSU fell to 2-1, while Kiffin's former team improved to 3-0.

articles.title: Bayern Munich News: FC Bayern not actively pursuing Liverpool star Florian Wirtz; Man City eyeing BVB’s Felix Nmecha; Tottenham Hotspur is melting down; and MORE!
articles.summary: Maybe one day FC Bayern will get Florian Wirtz.
articles.body:
Despite that TeamTalk report from last weekend, Sport Bild's Christian Falk says that Bayern Munich is not going to pursue a move for Liverpool attacker Florian Wirtz :

So, you can see where some reports have taken these conditions and claimed that one plus one equals two. Of course, if Florian Wirtz were, at some point in future, interested in making a return to the Bundesliga, Bayern Munich would be the first team he'd talk to. However, there is nothing planned. Bayern have a big squad and everyone's feeling really confident. Musiala has a long contract and don't forget that Vincent Kompany is trying a new system with Michael Olise as the fulcrum in the centre – the same position he currently plays in for the French national team . So, FC Bayern have a lot of options. Don't forget, either, that it was a lot of money Liverpool paid for Wirtz. ❌ It is NOT TRUE: Bayern Munich are tracking Florian Wirtz and could make a shock move for the Liverpool player. My information is that this is not true. Of course, there is a big history between FC Bayern and Wirtz. There were two secret meetings before he decided on Liverpool: the first one in Munich and then in Liverpool as well. At the time, Arne Slot persuaded the German international to switch to Merseyside. If there is such a connection, you're always going to have rumours – even more so when there are concerns over his performance levels in England. To be clear, I don't necessarily share those concerns; I think Wirtz is performing better than he did last year. He has a new position in the team. On the other hand, you have an ongoing topic with Jamal Musiala, where he's not in his best possible shape at the moment due to his illness following his injury struggles last year.

So, you can see where some reports have taken these conditions and claimed that one plus one equals two. Of course, if Florian Wirtz were, at some point in future, interested in making a return to the Bundesliga, Bayern Munich would be the first team he'd talk to. However, there is nothing planned. Bayern have a big squad and everyone's feeling really confident. Musiala has a long contract and don't forget that Vincent Kompany is trying a new system with Michael Olise as the fulcrum in the centre – the same position he currently plays in for the French national team . So, FC Bayern have a lot of options. Don't forget, either, that it was a lot of money Liverpool paid for Wirtz.

❌ It is NOT TRUE: Bayern Munich are tracking Florian Wirtz and could make a shock move for the Liverpool player. My information is that this is not true. Of course, there is a big history between FC Bayern and Wirtz. There were two secret meetings before he decided on Liverpool: the first one in Munich and then in Liverpool as well. At the time, Arne Slot persuaded the German international to switch to Merseyside. If there is such a connection, you're always going to have rumours – even more so when there are concerns over his performance levels in England. To be clear, I don't necessarily share those concerns; I think Wirtz is performing better than he did last year. He has a new position in the team. On the other hand, you have an ongoing topic with Jamal Musiala, where he's not in his best possible shape at the moment due to his illness following his injury struggles last year.

The reality of the situation is that Bayern Munich likely does maintain an ongoing interest in Wirtz (why wouldn't the Bavarians keep an eye on one of Germany 's top players?), but a move coming to fruition would be difficult right now or maybe even next summer.

First, Liverpool would not want to sell Wirtz at a discount barring some sort of total collapse this season. Second, Bayern Munich is not in need of another player at the moment, nor does it likely have all of its financial ducks in a row to make such a big move at the moment.

Maybe one day, Wirtz will suit up got Bayern Munich, but it probably won't happen any time soon.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha is off to a strong start this season and has reportedly drawn the interest of Manchester City and Liverpool:

Manchester City and Liverpool have been scouting a move for Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha. However, a January transfer is being ruled out.

Nmecha — and Borussia Dortmund, too — could both benefit from a good showing by Nmecha with Germany. As his reputation grows, BVB could be poised to make a financial windfall from the 25-year-old.

Bayern Munich just extended the contract of sporting director Christoph Freund, but Liverpool has a fondness for the front office member:

Liverpool are eyeing Christoph Freund, Bayern Munich's sporting director, as they assess potential candidates to replace Richard Hughes, although an internal appointment remains the most likely outcome at Anfield. FSG president Mike Gordon is now overseeing the search and is considering candidates from both within Liverpool's existing football structure and the wider market. Julian Ward, David Woodfine, Matt Newberry, and Pedro Marques are among the internal figures being assessed. However, Liverpool have also examined several senior football executives from across Europe and the Premier League, with Freund emerging as one of the more prominent continental names discussed. The 49-year-old is highly regarded across European football following his successful work with Red Bull Salzburg and Bayern Munich. He moved to Bayern in 2023 after building a strong reputation in Austria and has since held a key position within the German club's sporting structure. Liverpool's interest in the Bayern Munich executive would represent an ambitious option as FSG considers how to strengthen the club's football operation following Hughes' exit. However, there is an obvious obstacle to any potential move. Freund recently extended his Bayern contract until June 2029 and is not expected to leave the Bundesliga giants anytime soon. Liverpool would therefore face a significant challenge if they attempted to convince him to make the move to Anfield.

The 49-year-old is highly regarded across European football following his successful work with Red Bull Salzburg and Bayern Munich. He moved to Bayern in 2023 after building a strong reputation in Austria and has since held a key position within the German club's sporting structure.

Liverpool's interest in the Bayern Munich executive would represent an ambitious option as FSG considers how to strengthen the club's football operation following Hughes' exit. However, there is an obvious obstacle to any potential move.

Freund recently extended his Bayern contract until June 2029 and is not expected to leave the Bundesliga giants anytime soon. Liverpool would therefore face a significant challenge if they attempted to convince him to make the move to Anfield.

Freund has done well in his role under board member for sport Max Eberl, but he will always be scrutinized for his brief time in charge of personnel, which resulted in the signings of transfer busts Sacha Boey and Bryan Zaragoza .

Freund did also secure Eric Dier , a key player for a season-and-a-half at Bayern Munich, and Jonas Urbig , but the whole handling of that 2024 transfer window has left some soured on his ability to sit in the big chair — just not Liverpool it seems.

How are things going at Tottenham Hotspur ? Not great:

This is an extremely damning statement from Roberto De Zerbi — and probably not a great look for him either. Maybe worse, some players are going to be put off by this statement, which could make the situation even worse.

Arsenal winger Noni Madueke is getting interest from "several" Premier League clubs:

Several unnamed Premier League sides are monitoring the future of Noni Madueke as a January exit from Arsenal could be on the cards, according to Football Insider . The England international could leave the Emirates Stadium if the Gunners are open to it, as he is struggling for minutes in the early weeks of the season. Madueke, 24, only moved to Arsenal last summer from Chelsea , since when he has scored nine goals and registered four assists in 48 appearances. However, with youngster Max Dowman adding to the competition in his position on the right flank, another move could be on the cards.

FC Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick seems pretty thrilled with summer acquisition and Germany international Karim Adeyemi .

"I am very happy with Karim Adeyemi! He is lightning fast," said Flick. "His performance makes everything easier. I think he wasn't going through a good time in Germany and it did him good to change scenery and move to another country. I'm very happy that he chose us."

Flick is definitely a coach where wingers go to thrive.

articles.title: College football winners and losers: Losses by LSU and Texas A&M make Week 4 an already pivotal Saturday in the playoff race
articles.summary: Could Oregon, LSU or Texas A&M find themselves without much of a playoff path after Week 4?
articles.body:
Week 4 is shaping up to be an incredibly important week for the College Football Playoff.

It seems absurd to seriously think about the playoff before the calendar hits October. But No. 21 Oregon 's visit to No. 12 USC and No. 9 Texas A&M 's visit to No. 7 LSU are games that the selection committee could be referring to when deciding who's in and out in December.

We knew that one top-10 team in the SEC was going to lose in Week 3 as the Tigers visited No. 8 Ole Miss. And the Rebels got a 32-24 victory after LSU scored 17 straight to open the second half and tie the game.

LSU won't drop too far in Sunday's AP poll, but it now has very little margin for playoff error going forward. And it's facing a team that is in the same scenario three weeks into the season.

The Aggies entered Saturday as 17-point favorites over a Kentucky team that gave up 32 straight to Alabama in the second half of its Week 2 loss. The Wildcats were the more physical team on Saturday and pushed the Aggies around. The 31-21 win even led to Texas A&M coach Mike Elko immediately telling new Kentucky coach Will Stein that UK kicked the Aggies' butts in their postgame handshake.

Now, Texas A&M gets to go to Death Valley for a prime-time game. Whoever loses will be 2-2 and will probably have to go undefeated the rest of the way to make the playoff.

Yes, Alabama made the playoff at 10-3 a season ago. But the Tide's last loss of the season came in the SEC championship game. No team with three regular-season losses has made the 12-team playoff as an at-large through the first three seasons of the expanded playoff.

That could change in 2026. But neither LSU nor Texas A&M wants to bet on that.

The Aggies especially should be worried about their playoff fate. After making the playoff for the first time a year ago, they returned a roster capable of getting back to the playoff again. But Texas A&M's schedule required it to win games against unranked opponents like Kentucky.

After LSU, five of Texas A&M's final eight games are against teams currently ranked in the AP Top 25. And that group of teams includes three currently ranked in the top 15.

Oregon rebounded from its shocking loss to Oklahoma State in Week 2 with a program-record 84 points on Friday night against Portland State . And while the total was impressive — and likely cathartic for a Ducks program that dealt with many people watching the team's offensive film to see how obvious their tendencies were — it also came against an FCS opponent. Just three years ago, Oregon set its previous points record against that same team.

A loss to USC would put Oregon in a brutal playoff position, especially with a trip to Ohio State to come in November.

USC, meanwhile, can't afford the loss either. Not only do the Trojans have the Buckeyes on their schedule, but they have trips to No. 14 Penn State and No. 4 Indiana later in the season. Even if Oregon is ranked outside the top 10, this is the type of game Lincoln Riley's team needs to win to change the narrative around its competitiveness in the Big Ten.

Week 3 seemed massive because of the circus surrounding Lane Kiffin's return to Ole Miss. But what transpired on the field in Oxford and elsewhere on Saturday makes Week 4 even bigger. We can't wait.

Here are the rest of this week's winners and losers.

Mississippi State : The Bulldogs were outscored 13-0 by South Carolina in the first quarter on Saturday. They proceeded to go on a 41-10 run to put the game away in a 41-34 victory. MSU is now 3-0 as Kamario Taylor continues his star turn. The sophomore QB was 18-of-26 passing for 251 yards and four touchdowns and one interception and rushed eight times for 33 yards. South Carolina QB LaNorris Sellers threw two second-half interceptions and Mississippi State turned those turnovers into 10 points. The Bulldogs host No. 20 Missouri in Week 4 before Alabama visits to start October. Can Mississippi State be 4-0 when the Tide come to town?

Cincinnati : The Bearcats had an even bigger comeback win. Cincy was down 28-7 at halftime to Miami (Ohio) before outscoring the RedHawks 28-3 in the second half for a 35-31 win. Cole Tabb's 53-yard run with 1:29 to go turned out to be the game-winning score after Cincinnati was down by 10 with 13:51 remaining.

Georgia Southern transfer QB JC French IV was 31-of-43 passing for 309 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for another. The Bearcats have a fourth straight home game in Week 4 and it's their toughest test yet as Kansas State comes to town.

Toledo: The Rockets scoff at the comebacks Cincinnati and Mississippi State had. Toledo trailed Temple 42-28 with 6:40 to go and then turned the ball over on downs with 4:40 to go after Adjatay Dabbs was ruled short of the line to gain on fourth down.

Toledo's defense was able to force a three-and-out and then the fun happened. The Rockets went on a 10-play, 83-yard drive to cut the lead to seven with 1:05 to go. An onside kick was needed and, guess what? Toledo recovered that. Two plays later, John Alan Richter connected with Daryl Barnett Jr. for a 23-yard TD that tied the game with 54 seconds to go.

Toledo got the ball first in overtime and scored a touchdown in two plays. And so did Temple. But the Owls decided they wanted no more overtime and went for two. However, Ajani Sheppard's pass fell incomplete, and Toledo won 49-48.

Louisville : Are the Cardinals the biggest threat to Miami in the ACC? Louisville made a huge step toward the ACC title game with a 41-31 win over SMU. Lincoln Kienholz threw for two touchdowns and ran for another as the Cardinals rushed 37 times for 265 yards. SMU rushed for 257 yards itself, but Kevin Jennings threw two interceptions and also fumbled just short of the goal line when it appeared he had cut Louisville's lead to three pending the extra point with 2:53 to go.

Louisville and Miami do not play each other in the regular season and the Cardinals do not have a team in the AP Top 25 remaining on their schedule after games against Ole Miss and SMU in the first three weeks. It's not a stretch to think that Louisville will be favored in every game the rest of the season.

West Virginia QB Michael Hawkins: The Oklahoma transfer had the best game of his college career on Saturday night in the Mountaineers' 38-27 win over No. 25 Virginia. Hawkins was 10-of-17 passing for 190 yards and two touchdowns while rushing 18 times for 123 yards and three scores. West Virginia is now 3-0 ahead of Big 12 play and has a chance to be a sleeper mid-pack team in the conference.

NC State : It's impossible to not start this category with the Wolfpack, who fell to 1-2 in the most absurd fashion on Saturday afternoon. The thought process behind NC State's penultimate offensive play made sense. The execution did not.

With six seconds to go and the ball at its own 5-yard line, the play was for QB CJ Bailey to run into the end zone and take a sack as time expired. Given NC State was leading 31-28, the safety would cut the lead to one but still preserve the win.

By now, you know that Bailey's retreat to the end zone did not result in a safety. He fumbled the ball as he got hit and Vanderbilt recovered in the end zone for a 35-31 win.

Should Bailey have dropped to the ground sooner? Could he have thrown it away? Did the new NCAA rule giving an untimed down to a punt returner who makes a fair catch as time expires play a role in the decision for Bailey to take the sack?

All those questions are fair. And it's a play that other coaches will assuredly be sharing with their teams for the foreseeable future as an example of how not to execute a clock-killer at the end of the game.

Colorado : Any good vibes leftover from Colorado's Week 1 win over Georgia Tech disappeared in a 41-7 drubbing at Northwestern. Wildcats QB Aidan Chiles had five total touchdowns as he went 17-of-22 passing for 241 yards and three scores and rushed for two other touchdowns. The Buffs turned the ball over four times: JuJu Lewis threw two interceptions and Colorado's running backs fumbled twice. Big 12 play begins in Week 4 with a trip to Baylor , and then Texas Tech and Utah visit Boulder. The Buffs could be 2-4 ahead of Oklahoma State's visit on Oct. 24.

Kansas: The Jayhawks are also 1-2 after turning the ball over three times and failing on all three of their fourth-down attempts in a 24-17 loss to Arizona State in London.

The pivotal sequence came late in the first half. Matthew Gill was punting out of his own end zone but his punt went just 17 yards before going out of bounds with 25 seconds to go and KU leading 7-3. The poor punt gave ASU the ball at the KU 25-yard line and the Sun Devils scored on their first offensive play.

And ASU scored again to start the third quarter when Jaren Hamilton returned the second-half kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown. What was a four-point lead turned into a 10-point deficit, and Kansas was never able to recover.

Colorado were rocked by Northwestern on Saturday, 41-7, losing their first game of the season. After the contest, head coach Deion Sanders gave props to his coaching counterparts, including Northwestern offensive coordinator Chip Kelly.

"Great game by Northwestern," he told reporters. "... [Kelly] called a heck of a game. Flat-out butt-kicking. I'm gonna try my best to explain everything that I need to explain to you in the most polite manner I can at this point. But they played a heck of a game. Forced us to turn the ball over. Forced us into bad decisions. Forced us into doing things that aren't truly who we are. Four turnovers, 80 yards worth of penalties. You're not going to win."

Northwestern finished the game with 423 yards of total offense, just one turnover to Colorado's four and 36:53 in time of possession. It was, indeed, a butt-kicking.

It was Colorado's first loss of the season after consecutive wins and the schedule is only going to get tougher when the Big 12 slate starts next week, with the Buffs traveling to face Baylor. Sanders has plenty to clean up after Kelly and the Wildcats humbled them on Saturday.

articles.title: Trinidad Chambliss, Not Lane Kiffin, is the Biggest Story in College Football
articles.summary: Somehow, the greatest show of all was an afterthought all week long.
articles.body:
Somehow, the greatest show of all was an afterthought all week long.

Well, not somehow . We know exactly why.

Lane Kiffin does that. In fact, he's a master of it. Perhaps no personality in all of sports has mastered the art of reveling in the spotlight—good, bad, or in between—quite like him. This week was no different.

Lost in the hate, revenge and venom that blanketed Kiffin's much-anticipated Oxford return—a reunion serenaded with expletives from one sunrise to the next—we largely neglected the person who would actually decide the outcome of the most anticipated football game to date.

His name is Trinidad Chambliss. He's part quarterback, part magician.

He's now the favorite to win the Heisman—or at the very least, he should be—after conquering LSU to a 32-24 win, scoring the go-ahead touchdown deep in the fourth quarter.

In the first half, the game was lopsided in Ole Miss' favor thanks in large part to Chambliss' brilliance. The quarterback completed 21 passes for 248 yards and two touchdowns in the first 30 minutes, as an exasperated, animated Kiffin looked on in disbelief.

While the second half featured an inspiring surge by the Tigers, Chambliss' touchdown run made the ultimate difference. Overall, he finished with 363 passing yards and three touchdowns.

In doing so, he lifted Ole Miss, Kiffin's former team, to a 3-0 mark.

The spectacle that led up to this game- months upon months of wondering what this scene would look like- culminated in an electric scene. While cameras followed Kiffin's every move, the player he unearthed and molded led to his undoing.

A year ago, almost to the day, the Ferris State transfer was thrust into his first meaningful action at Ole Miss when the team's starting quarterback was injured.

A year later, Chambliss spoiled the man's return, who made his rise possible, delivering a performance that will be celebrated in Mississippi households for generations.

At this point, why should we be surprised?

The Division II transfer didn't just play well when he took over as Kiffin's QB last year; he thrived. An incredible regular season gave way to a dazzling postseason, one that saw Chambliss take down Tulane, Georgia and nearly Miami to make the national championship

In those three games, the QB was sensational. He extended plays with his legs, delivered fastballs in stride and found a way to create when plays were seemingly dead.

He was particularly excellent when Ole Miss was in disarray—a product of Kiffin's elongated decision to leave coupled with the drama and disruptions surrounding a team squarely in the College Football Playoff.

Coming into this season, the storyline surrounding his small-school arrival was long behind him. Instead, Chambliss was largely recognized as one of the best players in the sport. One could argue that his performance on Saturday night positions him squarely as the face of college football.

The fact that he beat Kiffin in such epic fashion makes it that much more captivating.

Whether he's embraced the title or not, Kiffin has reemerged as the sport's true villain yet again. LSU's overpowering win over Clemson in Week 1 only elevated his status, providing substance that his team could be forced from the start.

That moment made this week possible. Kiffin, to his credit, kept his team squarely in the game even when they fell behind early and a potential blowout loomed.

That wasn't to be, though Ole Miss found a way. There's no mystery how the Rebels arrived here. At the center of it all was a quarterback capable of seemingly anything.

It's hard to connect the dots that Kiffin himself has openly connected. He ultimately left Ole Miss for LSU largely because he believed the infrastructure in Baton Rouge could offer him a better chance to win national championships.

Perhaps, in time, that will prove true. One game won't dictate this decision. But at least for one night, a night that will live on for some time, Ole Miss proved him wrong.

Heading into Saturday, the spotlight was squarely on the man who made the scene possible. As both teams move beyond the drama, a new storyline has emerged.

Ole Miss has a player—the player—capable of making its biggest football dreams come true.

articles.title: Texas Longhorns didn't drop hammer on UTSA. Are there concerns entering SEC play? | Golden
articles.summary: Arch Manning did throw two touchdown passes but the Texas Longhorns offense was more sputtery than fans would have hoped with Tennessee next week.
articles.body:
It wasn't the quietest game week , but once the No. 1 Texas Longhorns got to their happy place, it was business as usual Saturday night.

One caveat regarding Austin's local tackle football team running its record to 3-0 with its 30-6 blowout of scrappy but outclassed UTSA : It wasn't the steamrolling that many expected, at least not from an offensive perspective. The Horns totaled 397 yards, but they were a sputtering 397 yards.

The first half was similar to last week in that the the score at the break read 20-3, the difference being it was the Horns striding into the locker room with the lead this time around. And in case you made a beer run to the fridge at intermission, yes, head coach Steve Sarkisian stuck around for the interview this time around.

The defense picked up where it left off in the second half last week when it held the Buckeyes to three second-half points, but there is some concern with star edge rusher Colin Simmons , who was spotted in street clothes in the third quarter with a protective boot on his foot.

No. 15 Tennessee , a 42-9 winner over Kennesaw State, will surely provide a sturdier test in Knoxville. Here's the question: Will this offense wake up before 100,000-plus at Neyland Stadium in the SEC opener? While the Horns were never threatened, this was never about beating UTSA. Week 3 was about improving. Offensively, that didn't happen on a consistent basis.

While young running back Derrek Cooper dazzled late with some good power running and his first career touchdown, Texas struggled in pass protection and red zone efficiency. Meanwhile, quarterback Arch Manning improved to 11-0 in home starts and took some nice shots downfield to electric wideout Cam Coleman - who caught a pair of touchdowns in the first half - but he also took the kind of shots that grandfather Archie warned him about, the sort that come from the guys looking to take your head off.

Manning literally lost his helmet on a third-down scramble, leading to a collective gasp from the 103,753 at Royal-Memorial Stadium.

He was fine, even if the overall numbers were meh. Manning finished 16 of 32 for 161 yards and the aforementioned scores - pedestrian numbers that will have to improve if the Horns are to live up to that lofty ranking.

The good thing about a win is that the coaching staff has the license to get after the troops even harder this coming week. The Horns, to a man, understand the stakes at play. Rallying to beat Ohio State took a mountain of pressure off the program's back because the unspoken goal is to finish 10-2 or better to ensure a spot in the College Football Playoff.

The Longhorns are in good shape, but the Tennessee showing had better be tidier, lest they will be looking at loss No. 1.

articles.title: Did we see an Ohio State hangover for No. 1 Longhorns, and other Texas vs UTSA observations
articles.summary: Did we just witness an Ohio State hangover for No. 1 Texas football? Yes, the Longhorns beat UTSA 30-6, but they hardly blew the Roadrunners away. What we sa...
articles.body:
Perhaps the emotions of last week's comeback thriller over Ohio State , coupled with Texas football 's ascension to the No. 1 ranking in the country, led to a week-long hangover. Maybe all the off-field distractions from the Arch Manning/Steve Sarkisian/Holly Rowe storyline took a heavy toll.

Whatever the reason, No. 1 Texas beat UTSA with relative comfort and ease, but also in the Longhorns ' least impressive offensive performance of the season.

Quarterback Arch Manning was just 16 of 32 for 161 yards and a couple of touchdowns, the Longhorns scored just one touchdown in four trips inside the red zone before adding a late score, finished with neither a 100-yard rusher or receiver, punted three times and had another drive end on a failed fourth down inside the 20 in a perfunctory 30-6 win over the Roadrunners at Royal-Memorial Stadium.

"I just thought we were a little sloppy offensively," Texas coach Steve Sarkisian told the SEC Network+ sideline reporter immediately after the game.

Texas (3-0) can't afford such offensive doldrums next week in its SEC opener at Tennessee .

Here are some observations we saw from Saturday's win:

Colin Simmons ' injury a concern for Texas

The Longhorns better hope the injury to Colin Simmons isn't serious. Texas' All-American edge rusher picked up his second sack of the season in the first half but spent the second half in street clothes on the sideline with a boot on his right foot. Simmons remains one of the most disruptive forces in college football, and the Longhorns would miss his presence as they enter SEC play.

Texas' top two tacklers were linebacker Rasheem Biles and defensive back Kade Phillips . Simmons had the defense's lone sack.

Who's No. 1? How the top five teams fared Saturday

No. 2 Georgia beat Arkansas 47-17 in Fayetteville

No. 3 Notre Dame beat Michigan State 27-10 at home

No. 4 Indiana beat Western Kentucky 38-0 at home

No. 5 Miami beat Wake Forest 33-20 on the road Friday night

The Longhorns open their SEC schedule next week at No. 15 Tennessee; Georgia hosts No. 24 Oklahoma .

Third-down plays power Texas' dominant defense

The defense picked up the offense's slack while only allowing 143 total yards. The Longhorns solved their third-down woes - UTSA converted just one of its 11 third-down plays and veteran quarterback Owen McCown passed for only 70 yards for the game (and the Roadrunners rushed for only 73).

The Longhorns held the Roadrunners to one field goal in the second quarter and one field goal in the third.

Defense travels, which should give the No. 1 Longhorns some optimism on their first road trip of the season next week.
