articles.title: Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss overcome late rally from Lane Kiffin and LSU to win grudge match in 32-24 thriller
articles.summary: Chambliss was the hero of the day for the Rebels, leading a clutch touchdown drive before the Ole Miss defense held off the Tigers to win it in the final min...
articles.body:
OXFORD, Miss. — There's a campaign sign all over Oxford these days: TRINIDAD / KEWAN 2026. Based on how Saturday night at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium went, that ticket would win every vote in Mississippi outside of Starkville.

Led by Trinidad Chambliss (33 of 48, 363 passing yards, three total TDs), Ole Miss beat LSU 32-24. Running back Kewan Lacy, before he left the game with an injury, gashed LSU for another touchdown. That's one hell of a winning duo.

Maybe even more impressively, Ole Miss reduced the headline-dominating Lane Kiffin to an afterthought, sending him hustling out of Oxford once again despite a late Tiger surge.

Chambliss was the hero of the day for the Rebels, leading a clutch touchdown drive and scoring on a bootleg with just over five minutes left in the game. Ole Miss then converted on the 2-point attempt to extend its lead to eight points.

The Rebels' defense still had more work to do, and Sam Leavitt was more than game in leading the Tigers down for a potential game-tying score. But ultimately, Leavitt's third-down pass from the 6-yard line fell incomplete and then Ole Miss' Jaylon Braxton intercepted the fourth-down attempt after the pass was tipped to give the Rebels bragging rights in the bitter rivalry.

"It was a full circle moment for a lot of people," Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding said after the game. "No player, no person was bigger than anybody else. This place has been built the right way with really good people."

Ole Miss and LSU started playing the Magnolia Bowl way back in 1893. (Ole Miss won that one, 26-6.) Over the course of 113 more meetings since then heading into Saturday, they've each authored dramatic victories and suffered humiliating defeats. But through it all, through Billy Cannon's Halloween Run and The Night The Clock Stopped, through Archie and Eli, there had never been a game between these two quite like Saturday's … because they'd never shared a coach quite like Kiffin.

You know the story. Kiffin spent the last few weeks of the 2025 regular season — arguably the finest in Ole Miss history — flirting with the LSU job. When he did decamp to Baton Rouge, wrangling several of his staff and Ole Miss players along with him, Ole Miss, to quote that Michael Jordan meme, took that personally.

After Kiffin skipped town, the Rebels reached the CFP semifinals … and then circled Kiffin's return to Oxford on Saturday night on their calendars in blood. And once the day came around, Oxford showed out when Kiffin showed up.

An estimated 300,000 people flooded into Oxford on Saturday for the game. Very much related: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium has a capacity of 64,038. That meant tens of thousands of rabid Rebels, with a smattering of Tigers, swarmed every restaurant, bar, tailgate and port-a-john in town, starting almost as soon as the sun rose. By the time kickoff finally came around at 6:49 p.m. Central, all 300,000 — whether inside or outside the stadium — were amped to the gills. (Excluding the ones who went a little too hard too early, of course.)

Kiffin and LSU entered the field to a cascade of boos as loud as Vaught-Hemingway has likely ever managed. "It was different seeing him run out, and seeing him in the purple and gold, and seeing some of the other coaches on the other sideline for the other team," Chambliss said afterward. "But at the end of the day, it's just football. It's a game. And we're competitors."

Both teams started rocky, three-and-out'ing with negative yardage. But on their second possession, the Rebels found their footing, covering 59 yards in 12 plays to get on the board with a field goal. And from there, Chambliss went to work, leading the Rebels to touchdowns on three straight drives.

With precision, touch and guts large enough to be seen from space, Chambliss threaded passes over, around and through LSU defenders. This was the kind of performance that made Kiffin bring him to Oxford in the first place, and the kind of performance that Chambliss had hoped to post when he sued his way back into college football .

LSU, meanwhile, struggled on offense early, unable to move the ball with any consistency or regularity. Sam Leavitt spent most of the first half on the run, stymied by the Ole Miss defense at every turn. And even when he had opportunities, he struggled to close the deal, air-mailing a wide-open receiver in the end zone, among other sins. As a result, LSU fell behind 17-0, and the Lane-haters partied in the stands.

When LSU did finally score, in part because of a 75-yard lateral scramble by Leavitt that set up a Dilin Jones dive from the 2-yard line with less than two minutes remaining in the first half, Ole Miss quickly responded with an eight-play, 75-yard touchdown drive that ate up the rest of the half. With 30 minutes done, the Rebels led the Tigers 24-7, and the parties resounded from the stadium to the Grove to the Square.

After four straight scoring drives, Chambliss made his first error midway through the third quarter, and it was a costly one — an interception that LSU flipped into a touchdown. After forcing Ole Miss into a missed field goal, the Tigers again stormed down the field, culminating the drive with a beautiful pitch-and-catch from Leavitt to Ole Miss transfer Winston Watkins Jr.

And just like that, the Tigers were back within three … and as the third quarter wrapped up Vaught-Hemingway was very, very quiet. Less than four minutes later, the Tigers tied it at 24 with a field goal, capping a run of 17 straight points of their own.

Along the way, Ole Miss lost Lacy, who left the game with what Ole Miss described as an "upper body injury." Lacy had appeared to land hard on his left shoulder, the same shoulder he'd injured during the College Football Playoff badly enough to require surgery.

With just over 11 minutes left in the game and the score tied, Chambliss had to figure out how to leave behind his woeful third quarter and recapture the magic of the first half.

Chambliss marched the Rebels down the field in a 13-play drive that took more than six minutes off the clock, ran the ball in himself, and then pulled off a daring, opportunistic two-point conversion to take an eight-point lead. When LSU's desperation drive ended in the end zone interception, so too did the last of the Tigers' hopes.

"I don't think anybody came here to beat LSU," Golding said. "Is it sweet? Absolutely, and we'll enjoy it tonight for sure. But we've got to come back and work hard. We've got a really, really good Florida team next week. It wasn't the Super Bowl, and we didn't make it out to be the Super Bowl."

Stadium video screens warned the gleeful Ole Miss students against rushing the field, and they complied. But the Ole Miss band mockingly played "Neck," the unofficial LSU anthem, along with other inside jokes. In his postgame euphoria, Chambliss cursed during his interview with ESPN's Holly Rowe, then apologized an hour or so afterward, unnecessarily.

Kiffin himself hustled off the field in a hurry, accompanied by a battalion of police. This time, the Ole Miss fans were smiling as he left.

articles.title: Caden Clark scores stoppage-time goal for Sounders in 3-3 tie with Rapids
articles.summary: Caden Clark subbed on in the 83rd minute and scored in the third minute of stoppage time for the Seattle Sounders in a 3-3 tie with the Colorado Rapids on Sa...
articles.body:
COMMERCE CITY, Colo. (AP) — Caden Clark subbed on in the 83rd minute and scored in the third minute of stoppage time for the Seattle Sounders in a 3-3 tie with the Colorado Rapids on Saturday night.

Cristian Roldan scored his first goal since April 18 in the 49th minute and Dejan Joveljic added a goal in the 79th for Seattle.

The Sounders (7-9-8) are winless in 13 straight but unbeaten in their last five.

Morgan Whittaker scored his first two MLS goals and Donavan Phillip also scored his first career goal for Colorado.

Clark, near the top of the penalty arc, skipped a shot past diving goalkeeper Nico Hansen and inside the left post for his first goal since 2024 for Montreal. Clark, a 23-year-old midfielder, was acquired Sept. 1 in a trade with D.C. United .

Phillip gave the Rapids (11-12-3) a 2-1 in the 56th minute. Loïc Williams flicked a header, off a corner kick played in by Whittaker, that was parried by goalkeeper Andrew Thomas, but Phillip slammed home the putback to make it 2-1.

Whittaker redirected a cross played by Paxten Aaronson into the net from near the penalty spot to open the scoring in the 28th minute. The 25-year-old Whittaker was acquired Sept. 4 and made his debut for the Rapids when he subbed on in the 54th minute of Colorado's 1-0 win over Montreal last Saturday.

Whittaker took a pass from Aaronson, gently chipped his first touch to himself and then blasted it out of the air and off the crossbar into the net to make it 3-1 in the 76th minute.

Rapids: Visit the LA Galaxy next Saturday.
